payload.name: EnumerationHowQuestionsFollowUp
payload.description: When a user asks how a person achieved, promoted, created, or improved something (an enumeration 'how' question) and the initial memory search returns mostly general statements about the person/entity, run additional targeted searches for that person's specific actions or events before answering.
content: Detect enumeration-type 'how' questions ('How did X promote/start/improve/create...?') that ask for concrete steps or methods; do not treat general state or status memories as a complete answer.

After the first retrieval, if the question implies multiple methods and the evidence contains few distinct event/action memories about the subject, run at least one follow-up search: pair the subject with action-oriented terms (made, created, developed, launched, partnered) or use a structured search of event memories filtered by subject and sorted by recency; merge results before the sufficiency check.
Stop after one or two follow-ups when no new distinct actions appear or each relevant time period has at least one concrete method; do not exhaustively list all memories.

solves: For 'how did X do Y' questions, the agent may answer from top-k general memories and miss specific action/event memories that lack the question's keywords. This skill applies when a future question asks for a person's methods or steps (e.g., promote, create, improve, start a business) and the first search returns mostly state summaries; it instructs the agent to run follow-up targeted/structured searches for the subject's concrete events before judging sufficiency. It must not apply to questions answered by a single fact or descriptor where the initial retrieval already suffices.
